description: Ми — Astrognomes, команда допитливих і творчих людей, яких об’єднує любов до астрономії, програмування та науки. Ми захоплюємося дослідженням Всесвіту, створенням нових ідей, технологіями та дизайном. Шукаємо однодумців, які мають навички програмування, творчий підхід, інтерес до астрономії чи фізики, вміють працювати в команді або прагнуть навчатися. Неважливо, чи ви вже експерт — головне, цікавість, ініціативність і бажання створювати щось незвичайне разом!
summary:
Step into Space: Mission Architect is an educational browser game in which the player designs their own spacecraft and completes nine missions, from a first cubesat to a flight to Pluto.

The player chooses a camera, solar panels, a battery, an antenna, radiation protection, a heat shield or an RTG, and a rocket, and then launches the spacecraft. The simulation calculates mass, budget, the power balance including a planet's shadow, data volume, radiation and heating. If the engineering decisions are wrong, the spacecraft is lost, and the mentor, Dr. Olena Koval, explains the reason. During the missions, unexpected events occur: a solar flare, a dust storm, a computer failure.

The game teaches engineering thinking without textbooks: trade-offs between weight, cost and capability, balancing systems, and working within constraints. Students learn from their mistakes instead of memorizing facts. This makes space engineering understandable and engaging for schoolchildren.

The project runs in a single HTML file with no server, has three languages (Ukrainian, English, German), progression with upgrades, character customization, and multiplayer for up to four players.
details:
"Step into Space: Mission Architect" is an educational web game. Players build their own spacecraft (camera, panels, battery, antenna, platform, orbit, rocket) and complete nine missions, from a first cubesat all the way to Pluto. The simulation checks mass and budget, the power balance including a planet's shadow, data volume against antenna capacity, radiation, and heating near the Sun. If a design decision is wrong, the spacecraft is lost, and the mentor, Dr. Olena Koval, explains why. In flight, unexpected events occur: a solar flare, a dust storm, a computer failure.

The game requires no prior knowledge: concepts are introduced through analogies and short questions. Players learn from their mistakes. It features progression (upgrades bought with earned funds, astronaut customization, mission scoring), three difficulty levels, three languages (Ukrainian, English, German), and multiplayer for up to four players. Everything runs in a single HTML file, with no installation and no server.

The game makes space engineering understandable for students and raises interest in STEM. It shows the key principles of real missions: every kilogram has a price, systems depend on one another, and autonomy and redundancy are needed at great distances.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript without libraries, using Canvas, SVG, Web Audio and WebRTC. The AI assistants Gemini and Claude were used as development aids.

The chapters increase in difficulty: each new planet adds a new engineering problem. The game has a narrative, events and customization, and all graphics and sound are created entirely in code. We considered ease of entry for beginners, accessibility (mobile support, three languages) and privacy: data is stored only locally. The numbers in the game are simplified and are not real NASA data.
dataRefs: Parker Solar Probe (chapter “Touch the Sun”). This page describes the shield that keeps the instruments at about 85 °F (≈29 °C) while the shield itself reaches ≈2,500 °F, and the fact that it must be lightweight. According to NASA, the carbon foam core of the shield is 4.5 inches thick, i.e. ≈11 cm. This matches the name “Composite shield (11 cm)” in our game.
RTGs and New Horizons (chapters “The Red Planet”, “Edge of the Solar System”). NASA Science, “After 60 Years, Nuclear Power for Spaceflight Is Still Tried and True”.
RTGs and New Horizons (chapters “The Red Planet”, “Edge of the Solar System”). NASA Science, “How Does an RTG Work? The Seebeck Effect”.
RTGs and New Horizons (chapters “The Red Planet”, “Edge of the Solar System”). NASA, MMRTG factsheet (PDF).
Dust storm on Mars (chapter “The Red Planet”). NASA Science, “10 Things: Massive Dust Storm on Mars”.
Dust storm on Mars (chapter “The Red Planet”). JPL, “Opportunity Hunkers Down During Dust Storm”.
Dust storm on Mars (chapter “The Red Planet”). NASA SVS, “Mars 2018 Global Dust Storm”.
Radiation near Jupiter (chapter “Giant Jupiter”). NASA/JPL, “Juno Armored Up to Go to Jupiter”. This page describes Juno’s radiation vault. In the game, it corresponds to the “Rad-hard platform”.
projectRefs: Gemini (Google), AI assistant, used for help with the project idea.
Claude (Anthropic), AI assistant for help with code and texts.
Canvas 2D API (all graphics: planets, spacecraft, rocket, animations).
Web Audio API (all sounds and background music are generated in code, with no audio files).
WebRTC API (serverless multiplayer through code exchange).
Compression Streams API (compression of room codes for multiplayer).
Web Storage API (saving the player’s progress in the browser).

Google’s public STUN server stun.l.google.com:19302, used by multiplayer to connect players. It is the only external service, and it transmits only technical network data, not any game content. General reference for the technology.
